airport.name: Pine Bluff Regional Airport, Grider Field

summary: Pine Bluff Regional Airport, Grider Field (PBF/KPBF) is a public-use airport located approximately 5 miles southeast of Pine Bluff, Arkansas, serving the broader southeast Arkansas region. Originally established as a military training facility during World War II, the airport now functions primarily as a general aviation facility with historical ties to the Grider family and the local community. It features a single main runway capable of handling regional aircraft and provides essential air access for business, medical, and recreational aviation in the Arkansas Delta region.
faqs:
Q: What is the main runway at Pine Bluff Regional Airport?
A: The airport has a primary asphalt runway (18/36) that is approximately 6,000 feet long, suitable for regional jets and general aviation aircraft.

Q: Does Pine Bluff Regional Airport offer commercial airline service?
A: Scheduled commercial passenger service has been very limited in recent years; the airport primarily serves general aviation, charter flights, and air cargo operations.

Q: Are there any military connections to the airport?
A: Yes, the airport has historical ties to World War II-era military aviation training and continues to support some military flight operations in the region.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The airport offers fuel services, aircraft maintenance, hangar rentals, and tie-down spaces for general aviation users, along with a terminal building for passengers and pilots.
transport_tips: The airport is most easily accessed by personal vehicle, with rental car services available from regional providers in Pine Bluff. It is located off US Highway 65, approximately a 10-15 minute drive from downtown Pine Bluff. Taxi and rideshare options may be limited, so arranging ground transportation in advance is recommended for visitors without a vehicle.
local_tip: Frequent visitors recommend calling ahead for fuel availability and tie-down reservations, especially during the busy spring planting season when agricultural aviation traffic increases throughout the Arkansas Delta region.
